documents.stance_why: The page sets no campus rule for students; it tells instructors to "Define clear boundaries for AI use in course assignments and assessments" and advises against "a blanket AI policy", so the decision is delegated to instructors.
documents.summary: CITL's campus teaching guidance frames generative AI as a transformative force faculty should engage with, listing faculty uses (drafting syllabi, rubrics, quiz items) and student learning uses (tutoring, study aids, brainstorming, writing support). It asks instructors to set clear course boundaries rather than a blanket syllabus ban, require citation of AI-generated content, attend to accuracy, privacy/FERPA, access and IP, and redesign assignments toward presentations, visible and multimodal work. It sets no campus-wide rule for students.

documents.stance_why: The project requires AI: "an AI coding agent will write most of your code, and we expect it to", and students "need to purchase a Claude Pro subscription"; homework and quizzes ban AI-written code, but the required AI project drives the stance.
documents.summary: The CS 124 Fall 2026 syllabus splits the course into two regimes: homework and CBTF quizzes (70% of the grade) where all code must be written by the student and AI may only explain concepts, and an independent project where an AI coding agent (Claude Code, via a paid Claude Pro plan) is expected to write most of the code. The project is graded on hours of engaged work measured from Claude Code session activity, and its integrity rules target misrepresenting engagement (tampering with logs, others running sessions), backed by automated checks of transcripts and code.
